question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined phrase in the given sentence.

When it comes to negotiations, he knows how to __act in a way that maximises his advantages__ and get the best deal.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e., **play his cards right**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Play his cards right"** refers to using one's resources or strategies wisely to achieve the best possible outcome. (समस्याओं से निपटने के लिए समझदारी से काम करना)

 
 
• **Example:** If he **plays his cards right**, he could become the next CEO of the company.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiom for maximizing advantages in negotiations is **'play his cards right'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **play his cards right**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Play it safe** (सावधानी से खेलना): Acting cautiously and avoiding risks.

 
 
• **Example:** She always prefers to **play it safe** when trying new things.
 
 
 
• **Play it by ear** (अनुमान के आधार पर कार्य करना): To act spontaneously and according to the situation without a fixed plan.
 
 
• **Example:** Let's not plan everything in detail now, we'll just **play it by ear**.
 
 
 
• **Play it by air** (हवा में खेलना): This phrase is typically a mistaken version of "play it by ear" and does not have a recognized idiomatic meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect usage: He decided to **play it by air** and see what happens during the trip. Correct usage: He decided to play it by ear and see what happens during the trip.
